newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Yugo cen.bank to keep dinar rate fixed - governor.
newsitem.headline: Yugo cen.bank to keep dinar rate fixed - governor.

text.p: The Yugoslav central bank will not change the dinar's exchange rate before the end of the year, leaving it fixed at 3.3 per German mark, a central bank official said on Friday.
"Nothing would justify any change in the current dinar exchange rate and we are determined to keep it at this level," the central bank vice-governor Ratko Banovic told Reuters.
According to Banovic, the National Bank of Yugoslavia (NBY) has sufficient currency reserves, higher than at the beginning of the year, to defend the dinar.

He declined to give the reserves' figure, but last May the then central bank governor Dragoslav Avramovic announced the currency reserves stood at about $330 million. Since then, no data has been released.
Banovic dismissed recent calls for the dinar devaluation to help stimulate exports.

"There is no reason for a devaluation because the dinar is still undervalued by 6 percent," he said, adding that even if the central bank devalued, it would offer only short-term relief for exporters.
"When the central bank last devalued the dinar in November 1995, it was aware that the realistic exchange rate would be 2.4 per German mark," Banovic said.
But he said the central bank did not want to take risks and added breathing space by fixing the dinar at 3.3 per mark.

"The current exchange rate is also supported by the uninterrupted activity of the local interbank forex market, where the National Bank of Yugoslavia intervenes every day to prevent the exchange rate fluctuating," he said. -- Gordana Filipovic, Belgrade newsroom, +381 11 222 4254
